structured_output.conclusion:
On 14 May 2024 the jury trial in Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417) was under way and liability was undecided.

Qorvo claims Akoustis was unjustly enriched by $66.1 million through a head start from misappropriated trade secrets, and it seeks enhanced damages. By D.I. 590 the jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable UDTPA damages. Akoustis disputes any damages, and its general counsel said an eight-figure verdict is possible if the jury adopts Qorvo's experts' theories.

Akoustis had $15.2 million of cash at March 31, 2024 and reports substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. It states that an adverse judgment would reduce its runway and could lead it to curtail or cease operations and file for bankruptcy protection. Apart from $48.0 million of ATM capacity, it has no committed funding.

Under the indenture (eff_003), final money judgments above $10.0 million (excluding insured amounts) that remain unpaid or unstayed for 60 days are an Event of Default after notice. The trustee or holders of 25% may then declare the $44.0 million of notes due. If the stock is delisted after the October 21, 2024 Nasdaq compliance deadline, holders may require a cash repurchase at 100% of principal (eff_008).

No accrual has been recorded for the Qorvo claims, so the baseline is unchanged (eff_006). The verdict and its consequences are carried by dispute_001 and financing_001.

The pivotal unknowns are the verdict amount and its timing, any insurance or stay, and Akoustis's cash and ATM proceeds at the time of the verdict.
pivotal_unknowns: The jury verdict in Qorvo v. Akoustis: liability, the unjust-enrichment, exemplary and patent amounts, and the entry date of judgment
Whether a judgment over $10.0M would be covered by insurance or stayed by bond, which determines whether the notes' 60-day judgment-default clock runs
Akoustis's cash at the verdict date and realised ATM proceeds relative to its operating burn and the line's installments
Whether Akoustis regains Nasdaq bid-price compliance by October 21, 2024 (reverse split), avoiding the holders' cash repurchase right on $44.0M of notes
